key_insight: The paper shows that lithium-ion battery health can be estimated jointly for remaining useful life and capacity using only partial-charging data, without needing historical full-cycle capacity labels. It combines recent charging behavior with degradation trends through a cross-expert model to improve battery prognostics.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of predicting battery remaining useful life and capacity when full-cycle capacity measurements are unavailable or costly to obtain. The method is designed for realistic settings where only partial-charging measurements from recent cycles are available.
method: Uses partial-charging measurements from nominal 10-minute segments sampled across a 30-cycle history.
Encodes degradation patterns with a pretrained GRU-based RUL expert to capture long-term temporal behavior.
Uses a second expert with 2D-CNN features to extract local charge-pattern information from recent battery behavior.
Combines the experts in a cross-expert framework to jointly predict remaining useful life and capacity.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical prognostics approach for real battery systems where labels are sparse or expensive. It can improve maintenance planning and battery management using data that is easier to collect in the field.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing partial-charging inputs flowing into two expert branches and a joint output head.
A timeline graphic of 30 cycles highlighting ten sampled 10-minute segments.
An architecture block diagram for GRU + 2D-CNN cross-expert fusion.
A comparison chart showing predicted vs. actual RUL and capacity over battery degradation.
paper_title: Joint Remaining Useful Life Prediction and Capacity Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries Using Partial-Charging Data
paper_authors: Khoa Tran, Ho-Si-Hung Nguyen, Phone Wai Yan Moe, Hung-Cuong Trinh, Thi-Hoang-Giang Tran
